issues.problem: Describes the pointer ownership rules that plan-review round 1 rejected, not the ones that shipped. It says 'a dangling link of other text is an earlier pointer and is `updated`' and that only 'a link of theirs that resolves' is skipped. Disposition 14 (decision 07:26:47.122Z, findings 1, 17, 18) made every link of other text the user's, dangling or not, so init skips it and never replaces it. The built code agrees: POINTER_TEXTS_PAST is empty (hosts.mjs:57), and readPointer (doctor/hosts.mjs:107) classes any other text as `theirsLink`, which doctor reads as WARN.
issues.suggested_fix: Rewrite the ownership sentence: a link of our shape that resolves is kept; ours and not resolving is WARN not installed, or retargeted when it is misdirected; a text in POINTER_TEXTS_PAST (empty in this stage) is an earlier pointer; any other link, dangling or resolving, or a real file or directory, is the user's: skipped, WARN naming it.
issues.failure_scenario: A maintainer reading the closeout expects init to overwrite a user's dangling link, which is the destructive behaviour the plan review removed.
